'''Muhammad Ibrahim''' ({{langx|bn|মুহাম্মদ ইব্রাহীম}}; born 1 December 1945) is a Bangladeshi academic.<ref name="man">{{Cite news |author=Apurba Jahangir |author-link=Apurba Jahangir |date=2015-01-24 |title=A man of science |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/a-man-of-science-61397 |access-date=2018-05-29 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref> He is a former professor of physics at [[University of Dhaka]].<ref name=man/> He is the moderator of the show ''Desh o Biggyan'' on [[Bangladesh Television]]. He is the editor of ''Bigyan Shamoiki'', the first monthly science magazine of Bangladesh.<ref name=man/> Since January 2015, he has been serving as a professor of the General Education Department at [[University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh]] (ULAB).<ref name=ulab>{{Cite news|url=https://ulab.edu.bd/2015/12/14/muhammad-ibrahim-new-head-of-general-education-program/|title=Muhammad Ibrahim new Head of General Education Program - University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh|date=2015-12-14|work=University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh|access-date=2018-05-29|language=en-US}}</ref>

Ibrahim is the recipient of [[Bangla Academy Literary Award]] (2006) in the science category.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2008/02/20/three-get-bangla-academy-award|title=Three get Bangla Academy Award|publisher=bdnews24.com|access-date=2018-05-29|date=2008-02-20}}</ref>

==Background and education==
The fourth of nine children,<ref name=family>{{Cite web|url=http://www.muhammadyunus.org/index.php/professor-yunus/78-about-professor-yunus-family|title=About Professor Yunus :: Family|last=Ansari|website=www.muhammadyunus.org|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-05-29}}</ref> Muhammad Ibrahim was born on 1 December 1945 in the city of [[Chittagong]], [[Bengal Presidency]]. He belongs to a [[Bengalis|Bengali]] family of [[Muslim]] [[Saudagar (surname)|Saudagars]] hailing from the village of Bathua, by the [[Kaptai road]] in [[Hathazari Upazila|Hathazari subdivision]].<ref name="$27">{{cite news |date=14 October 2006 |title=First loan he gave was $27 from own pocket |url=http://archive.thedailystar.net/2006/10/14/d6101401033.htm |newspaper=The Daily Star |access-date=22 August 2007 |archive-date=18 May 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518074321/http://archive.thedailystar.net/2006/10/14/d6101401033.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=Hero>{{cite news |last=Haider |first=Mahtab |date=1 January 2007 |title=Muhammad Yunus: The triumph of idealism |url=http://www.newagebd.com/2006/dec/28/newyear07/heroes01.html |work=New Year Special: Heroes |publisher=New Age |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070107075121/http://www.newagebd.com/2006/dec/28/newyear07/heroes01.html |archive-date=7 January 2007 |access-date=11 September 2007}}</ref> His father was [[Dula Mia Saudagar|Haji Muhammad Dula Mia Saudagar]], a Sufi jeweller, and his mother was Sufia Khatun. One of his elder brothers is ex-Chief Advisor [[Muhammad Yunus]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news/yunus-centre-protests-finance-ministers-statement|title=Yunus Centre protests Finance Minister's statement|date=2013-07-03|work=The Daily Star|access-date=2018-05-29|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thedailystar.net/showbiz/showbiz-column/television-lifetime/television-innovation-1206286|title=Television of Innovation|date=2016-04-09|work=The Daily Star|access-date=2018-05-29|language=en}}</ref> By 1949, his mother was afflicted with psychological illness.<ref name="Hero"/>  He studied at the [[Chittagong College]]. Around 1962, he got admitted into the physics department of the [[University of Dhaka]] where he completed his bachelor's and master's in 1965 and 1966 respectively. He earned his [[Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Southampton]] on surface physics in 1972.<ref name=family/>

His siblings were in order; Momtaz Begum, Muhammad Abdus Salam, [[Muhammad Yunus|Professor Muhammad Yunus]], Doctor Muhammad Ibrahim ''(self)'', Umme Kulsum, Muhammad Ayub, Muhammad Azam, Muhammad Jahangir, Muhammad Moinul Alam<ref>{{Cite web |date=2009-05-25 |title=About Professor Yunus :: Family |url=https://www.muhammadyunus.org/post/90/about-professor-yunus-family |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=www.muhammadyunus.org |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==
Ibrahim was a faculty member in University of Dhaka's Physics Department until he retired in 2012.<ref name=profile/> He served as the director of Renewable Energy Research Centre at the same university.<ref name=profile>{{Cite news|url=https://ulab.edu.bd/academics/faculty-list/profile/51/|title=Faculty Profile - University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh|work=University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh|access-date=2018-05-29|language=en-US}}</ref> He also served as a visiting professor in [[BRAC University]].<ref name=ulab/>

Ibrahim is the founder and executive director of Centre for Mass Education and Science (CMES), an [[NGO]] which aims to promote the use of science and technology at the root level.<ref name=man/><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cmesbd.org/index.php/about-us/history/|title=History|website=cmesbd.org|language=en-US|access-date=2018-05-29}}</ref>

==Awards==
* [[Bangla Academy Literary Award]] (2006){{citation needed|date=July 2024}}
* WorldAware Business Award (2004){{citation needed|date=July 2024}}
* Institute of Diploma Engineer Gold Medal (2000){{citation needed|date=July 2024}}
* Qudrat-E-Khuda Gold Medal (1989){{citation needed|date=July 2024}}
* Agroni Bank Award for Children Literature (1987)<ref name=family/>
